content_preview.summary: NYC will disable AI in 38 school tech contracts and ban student-facing chatbots through 8th grade, in what Mayor Mamdani calls the nation's broadest school AI moratorium.

No suspicious_patterns flagged in the manifest for any of the three snapshots. I decompressed and read the full extracted text of all three snapshots (not just excerpts) and cross-checked every factual claim, statistic, and direct quote in the submission body against them: (1) source-0 (2026/09/02, 'What to know about NYC's new AI ban and screen time limits') supports the core policy details — the 38 disabled ed-tech contracts, Amira (222 schools) and HMH 'Into Reading' AI turn-off, the Gemini ambiguity, the 5 high school AI pilot programs (Quill, Edia, Brisk Teaching, Playlab, Intel AI-Ready Schools) capped at 50,000/17% of high schoolers, the two 45-minute AI literacy modules, the screen-time tiers by grade band, the disability/ELL and assessment exemptions, the teacher use rules, the $25,000 purchase-review threshold and Lindsey Oates quote, the advocacy coalition's 'step in the right direction' reaction, the Buery statement, the Mulgrew quote about enforcement falling to school communities, the Mamdani quotes on enforcement, and the 'What We Don't Know' claims about the undisclosed product list and the withheld AI-use survey across 1,600 schools — all verified verbatim or substantively accurate. (2) source-1 (2026/08/26, 'NYC schools head toward first day without gradebooks...') supports the Samuels-ordered July purchasing freeze, the 'missed the mark' quote, the anonymous Brooklyn principal's 'Two weeks before the start of school...' / 'It's a huge pain' quotes, and the Tom Liam Lynch quotes on late timing and pedagogy — all verified verbatim. (3) source-2 (2026/09/01, 'Fresh faces, AI fears: 4,000 new teachers...') supports the Barclays Center orientation, the ~6,600 teacher hiring target and ~1,100 Teaching Fellows cohort, the Jasmine Hall and Moshab Rahman quotes, and Mulgrew's 'How are we banning AI in a high school?' / 'The students are using it anyway' quotes from the prior day — all verified verbatim.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No hallucinated quotes or fabricated specifics found. Quote-attribution check requested for this review (correcting a prior Mulgrew→Buery misattribution) confirms the submission now attributes each quote correctly: the 'While well-intentioned, a blanket one-year AI ban...' line is correctly attributed to Richard Buery (Robin Hood Foundation CEO, former deputy mayor) per source-0, and the 'school communities or individual educators to figure out after the fact...' and 'How are we banning AI in a high school?' lines are correctly attributed to UFT President Michael Mulgrew per source-0 and source-2 respectively — matching the source text exactly in each case. Headline superlative check: the article's headline and body both attribute the 'broadest generative AI moratorium in the nation' characterization to Mamdani specifically (the summary reads 'in what Mayor Mamdani calls the nation's broadest school AI moratorium' and the Overview quotes it directly as his description), and source-0 confirms this is Mamdani's own on-record description as reported by Chalkbeat, not an independent ranking Chalkbeat itself verified. This is accurately sourced as an attributed claim rather than presented as fact-checked by the reporters; the headline omits the explicit 'Mamdani says' framing that the summary and lead carry, which is a minor stylistic tightness rather than a sourcing defect, since a reader reaches the attribution within the first sentence of the summary and body.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout. Presents both supportive (advocacy coalition) and critical (Buery, Mulgrew) reactions to the policy, plus operational friction (principals, Tom Liam Lynch) and grassroots uncertainty (incoming teachers). No editorializing language detected.

editor_notes.single_source_caution: All 3 sources are from a single outlet, Chalkbeat New York. Applied extra scrutiny per newsroom policy: Chalkbeat is a nonprofit, editorially independent education-specific newsroom (part of the Civic News Company alongside Votebeat and Healthbeat) with two named, bylined reporters (Michael Elsen-Rooney, Alex Zimmerman) and direct on-the-record quotes from named officials (Mamdani, Samuels, Brady, Oates, Buery, Mulgrew) and named private citizens (Hall, Rahman, Puleri). No evidence of cherry-picking, selective quotation, or distortion across the three pieces — the submission's claims track the source articles closely and proportionately. The chalkbeat.org domain is not yet in config/source_allowlist.txt, which is why the automated script flagged an allowlist warning and defaulted to APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS; this is a config-list gap, not a reputability problem (Chalkbeat NY is comparable in standing to the already-allowlisted Texas Tribune, a nonprofit regional/beat newsroom).
